purpose: ToggleGroup is a connected group of buttons that picks exactly one value out of a small set of related options, with a selection indicator that slides to the active segment. It renders as a `radiogroup` whose segments are `radio` buttons, is driven by an `options` array plus `v-model`, and works uncontrolled through `defaultValue`. It differs from `tabs`, which switches between content panels it owns: a segmented button only holds the chosen value and leaves rendering what that value means to the consumer.
useWhen: Switch in place between two to five related modes, views or ranges (a time range, a list/grid view, a filter scope) where exactly one is always active.
Offer a compact single choice in a toolbar or a card header where a radio list would take too much room.
Show a choice that is currently unavailable as a locked segment (`disabled` option) instead of hiding it.
avoidWhen: The choice switches between content panels that belong to the control → use `tabs`.
The choice is a form field with a label, helper text or validation → use horizontal `field`s with a `radio-button`, or `Field.Label` choice cards when each option needs a description.
The value is a binary on/off setting → use `switch` (in a horizontal `field` inside a form).
The user can pick more than one option → use `checkbox` (in a horizontal `field`).
The control triggers an action instead of holding a value → use `button` or `split-button`.
related: tabs` — tabs that own their panels; reach for it when each option reveals its own content region.
field` — a horizontal `Field` with a `radio-button` is the form-field single choice with label and description; a `Field.Label` choice card when each option carries a title and description.
button` — a lone action; the segments here hold a value instead of firing one.
bestPractices: Keep labels to one or two words: segments never wrap (`whitespace-nowrap`) and long labels truncate.
Give every option a unique `value`; values are coerced to strings and used as the list key and the selection identity, so duplicates collide.
Pass `ariaLabel` whenever no visible label names the group.
Use `fluid` to make the group fill a narrow container and share its width across segments, instead of styling the width at the call site.
Bind `v-model` when the selection lives in the parent; use `defaultValue` only to seed an uncontrolled group.
